title: 'Very early' to talk about permanent Liverpool move, says Araujo
subtitle: Having impressed early on in his loan spell with Liverpool, Ronald Araujo has been tipped to make his move to Merseyside permanent.
paragraphs: Ronald Araujo says it is still too early to discuss whether his loan move from Barcelona to Liverpool will become permanent at the end of the campaign.
Araujo joined the Reds on a season-long deal in August, when they were enduring something of an injury crisis in defence with Joe Gomez, Giovanni Leoni, Conor Bradley and Jeremy Jacquet all out.
Jacquet has recovered to make an excellent start to his Liverpool career, partnering Virgil van Dijk at centre-back, while Araujo has mostly featured at right-back.

No player has made more appearances for Liverpool this season than Araujo's 10 in all competitions (level with Jacquet and Alexis Mac Allister), and with Jeremie Frimpong suffering an injury during Saturday's 2-1 win at Brentford, his place in the team looks secure for now.

Eight of those appearances have been starts, and he has contributed to two clean sheets while contesting more aerial duels than any other Reds player (36, winning 25, the joint-most alongside Van Dijk).
Speaking ahead of Tuesday's Champions League meeting with Villarreal, Araujo acknowledged he is very happy at Anfield, though he does not know what the future holds.
"It's very early to talk about these things," Araujo told reporters. "I'm just trying to enjoy every day, continue to grow and develop every day to have that confidence.
"I'm really happy to be here, my family are also very happy, but it's a bit early to be talking about these things.
"I'm very happy because, since I arrived, I've been welcomed just as another player, not just by the people at the club but by the fans.
"I am very grateful to them. I want to give back to them by giving everything in training and every match."
Arajuo has won 35 of his 60 total duels in a Liverpool shirt, with only Jacquet (48), Mac Allister (40) and Milos Kerkez (39) winning more for the Reds this campaign.
